description:
## Outcome

        Jidoka emits a small versioned, JSON-projectable lifecycle event set for sessions, turns, models, tools, and automation cells through one failure-isolated dispatcher.

        ## Why now

        Extensions must observe the same runtime in interactive and automated modes. Event shape and order must be stable before the host executes handlers.

        ## Current state

        `Jidoka.Event` is a public turn-stream contract with atom event names and internal data rules. It is useful for the TUI but is not a language-neutral extension envelope. No dispatcher isolates extension subscriber failures.

        ## Ownership and boundary

        This is a `jidoka` change. Keep existing `Jidoka.Event` compatible. Add an extension-facing envelope and dispatcher. The CLI may originate automation cell boundary events through a public Jidoka call later, but it does not own the event schema.

        ## Detailed implementation

        1. Add a versioned envelope with schema, event ID, string event name, timestamp, session/request/turn references, extension namespace, and portable data.
2. Define the first event set: session start/resume/compact/end; turn start/update/end; model start/update/end/error; tool before/update/after/error; automation cell start/end.
3. Define exact ordering, terminal pairing, cancellation, hibernation, and error rules.
4. Add a dispatcher with ordered delivery per session and failure isolation between subscribers.
5. Bound event payload size and redact secrets before delivery.
6. Map current runtime events to the new envelope without changing turn semantics.
7. Let deterministic tests inject event IDs and time.

        ## Acceptance criteria

        - [ ] Every listed event has one documented portable shape and version.
- [ ] Events for one session preserve documented order.
- [ ] Cancellation, denial, hibernation, and error each produce one correct terminal path.
- [ ] One subscriber failure does not change the turn result or block another subscriber.
- [ ] Payloads use string keys and contain no live or secret values.
- [ ] Existing stream/TUI event tests remain compatible.

        ## Test plan

        - Success: deterministic complete session sequence with model and tool events in exact order.
- Invalid input: unknown event name, malformed references, nonportable data, and oversized payload.
- Runtime failure: subscriber raise, exit, timeout, and malformed return.
- Boundary and security: secret redaction and no subscriber ability to mutate an already emitted event.
- Deterministic capability: fixed clock/IDs plus fake subscribers, LLM, operation, and policy.
- JSONL and exit status: Jason round trip for every event; events never write CLI stdout directly.

        ## Documentation

        Add the event catalog, version policy, ordering table, and subscriber failure rules. Link streaming but keep the two contracts distinct.

        ## Non-goals

        Do not add custom event names. Do not persist a new event store. Do not add terminal rendering. Do not run process extensions.

        ## Dependencies

        Blocking issues:

        - `jido_cli-tqg.4.2` — Define trusted extension identity and permission bindings
- `jido_cli-tqg.2.1` — Add a public ordered Jidoka session sequence

        Features unlocked by this story:

        - Built-in extension hooks
- Process extension notifications
- Automation cell extension events

        ## Commit plan

        Create exactly one focused `jidoka` commit. Use a message such as `feat(jidoka): add extension lifecycle events (jido_cli-tqg.4.3)`. Do not include another backlog feature.

        ## Verification commands

        ```sh
        cd /Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_cli/jidoka
mix test test/jidoka/extension/event_test.exs test/jidoka/event_test.exs test/jidoka/stream_test.exs
mix quality
mix test
mix docs
        ```
title: Emit versioned portable extension lifecycle events
